title: Transient replica handovers and KV-ghost priming for SLA-safe onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Dedicated fleets sometimes experience brief throughput collapses during tenant onboarding or sudden traffic spikes because full weight residency + KV cache population takes several seconds to tens of seconds. Current warm-pool approaches either fully load weights (slow, expensive) or rely on cold-start fallbacks that reduce throughput and breach SLOs for committed customers.

Goal: Design and implement a low-cost, low-latency onboarding pattern that provides hard throughput guarantees during tenant handoffs by combining lightweight transient replicas, staged weight swap, and 'KV-ghost' priming (a thin, probabilistic KV cache snapshot used to serve warm prefixes while full KV hydration continues). The approach should integrate with existing autoscaler admission policies and Dedicated SLA accounting so we can provide predictable per-tenant throughput during the critical first N seconds after routing changes or scale-up events.
acceptance_criteria: Committed tenants (reserved capacity) experience <10% tail throughput degradation during onboarding compared to steady-state within the first 30s
Average cold-start token latency for synthetic onboarding workload reduced by >= 60% compared to baseline run (v1 warm-pool)
New transient replicas never exceed configured budgeted GPU memory footprint and are cleaned up within configurable TTL
Integration tests covering failure modes (replica crash during handover, stale KV snapshot) pass in CI and on a canary fleet
Runbook updated and postmortem hooks in Console for 'transient-handovers' events
design_notes:
Core concepts: 1) Transient replicas: short-lived, lightweight model processes instantiated with sliced attention kernels and compressed weight segments. They accept a limited fanout and act as an ingress buffer while full-weight nodes finish streaming. 2) Staged weight swap: weights are progressively atomically swapped in groups (embedding-blocks, attention-blocks) so early tokens route to a minimal-capacity runtime path while later tokens get full precision. 3) KV-ghost priming: create compact, lossy KV snapshots (top-k prefixes and hashed prefixes) derived from historical tenant traffic and recent global hot prefixes. Ghost snapshots are used for prefix hits with a probabilistic backoff for cache misses. 4) Policy integration: the autoscaler exposes a new admission-token that allows transient replica creation up to N per-fleet; the throughput-guarantee controller coordinates reservation tokens and chargebacks to tenant commitments.

Trade-offs considered: full-weight preloading gives best correctness but high cost; naive KV prewarming wastes GPU memory for rarely-used prefixes. Ghost priming is lossy (can cause small regressions for rare inputs) but acceptable for throughput guarantees and is gated per-tenant by quality budget.

Instrumentation: add metrics: transient_replica_count, transient_handovers, kv_ghost_hit_rate, staged_swap_progress, handover_throughput_ratio, handover_95th_latency. Emit structured events to Console with tenant_id, reservation_id, and handover_id for traceability.

comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to limit total transient replicas to 25% of fleet capacity by default. Ops requested a TTL default of 45s. Marco to draft admission API.

2026-02-27 - Marco Ruiz: Posted initial RFC draft: added sequence diagrams for staged weight swap. Requesting feedback on two open points: (1) whether to use compressed 8-bit segments for transient weights, (2) how to charge transient replicas to tenant reservations. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/engineering/dedicated/transient-handoffs#rfc

2026-03-01 - Priya Nair: Prototype boot times: transient replica context loaded in ~420ms on a40 with 8-bit segments; full-weight load still ~6.8s. Initial kv_ghost serialization (top-k = 10 prefixes) takes 120ms per shard.

2026-03-03 - Chen Zhao: KV summarizer uploaded; ghost snapshot size per-tenant ~1.2 MB (configurable). Noted edge-case when tenant has highly diverse utterances — mitigation: adaptive sampling of top prefixes.
2026-03-04 - Maya Singh: Dashboard draft pushed. Suggested metric 'handover_throughput_ratio' be normalized by reservation baseline; Ops wants an alert if ratio < 0.8 for >60s.

2026-03-05 - Security review (Emily Carter): Reviewed event schema and storage for ghost snapshots. No PII expected in ghost snapshots; recommended encryption-at-rest and explicit retention policy (30 days). Marking security_review_required = false after follow-ups.
